text: Blue-green deployment keeps two complete, independent environments running at once, with only one of them actually live at any moment.

Green, the new version, is fully deployed and verified before it receives a single real request. The cutover itself is just a routing change at the gateway from Lesson 13 -- not a redeploy -- so it's effectively instant, in either direction.

That speed isn't free. You're running both environments at full capacity during the overlap, which is double the compute. For a small service that's a rounding error -- for GPU-backed inference containers, it's a real, visible cost.

AI apps add a wrinkle a stateless web app doesn't have: blue and green can behave differently even with identical code, because of a different model checkpoint, a different inference library version, or a different GPU driver on the new instance type.

So a plain health check returning 200 isn't enough. Verifying green means running known test prompts through it and comparing outputs to blue's known-good results -- because a green service that's up but serving a different model is a worse failure than an outage.
Blue-green buys zero downtime at the cost of running two full environments. Next up: rolling updates, the cheaper alternative that doesn't need a second full environment at all.
